title: Background Remover with OpenCV GrabCut
description:
A small Python tool that removes the background from product photos and saves transparent PNGs, or JPGs on pure white for marketplaces. It uses OpenCV GrabCut and needs no model download and no GPU.

  • The first guess comes from the image border: pixels that look like the border color (in Lab color space) are probably background, the rest probably foreground, and a thin frame is always background.
  • GrabCut refines this guess with color models and a graph cut.
  • Clean-up: morphological opening and closing, filling of holes inside the product (light labels, reflections), optional "keep only the largest object", and a soft edge in the alpha channel.
  • Large photos are segmented on a downscaled copy for speed; the mask is scaled back to full size.

Works best for products on plain, light studio backgrounds. For busy backgrounds or hair and fur, a neural model such as rembg is the better choice.
implementationSteps: Install the two dependencies: pip install -r requirements.txt (OpenCV headless and NumPy).
Photograph products on a plain, evenly lit background and leave a margin around the product.
Estimate the background color from the image border and mark similar pixels as probable background, the rest as probable foreground.
Run cv2.grabCut with this mask (GC_INIT_WITH_MASK) for a few iterations on a copy downscaled to at most 1024 px.
Clean the mask with opening and closing, fill holes inside the product and, for single products, keep only the largest object.
Scale the mask back to full size and blur its edge slightly to get a soft alpha channel.
Save transparent PNGs, or composite on white and save JPGs with --white for marketplace main images.
Process a whole folder with python -m bgremove photos/ out/ and check the results; tune --tolerance for low-contrast products.
performance:
Expectations, not measured results:

  • Usually well under a second per photo on a laptop CPU at the default working size of 1024 px.
  • The tests require an overlap (IoU) of at least 0.9 between the mask and the true product shape on synthetic product photos.
  • Products whose color is very close to the background (white product on white) and fine structures such as hair need manual touch-up or a neural model.
userExperience: The user drops photos into a folder, runs one command and gets transparent PNGs (or white-background JPGs) with the same file names in the output folder. The command prints the foreground share per image, which makes failed cut-outs (0 % or almost 100 %) easy to spot.
